# HeartRateTap

> HeartRateTap is a browser wellness tool that estimates BPM from taps made while a person manually feels their own pulse; it is not a sensor or medical device.

## Product

- [Home — manual tap BPM estimator](https://www.heartratetap.com/): Use the tap tool, see the interval formula, review limitations, and keep a small local browser history.
- [Target heart rate calculator](https://www.heartratetap.com/target-heart-rate-calculator): Compare percent-of-maximum and heart-rate-reserve ranges with adjustable intensity inputs and visible formulas.
- [Heart rate recovery calculator](https://www.heartratetap.com/heart-rate-recovery-calculator): Calculate the BPM change after one or two minutes while retaining the measurement interval and protocol context.
- [HeartRateTap methodology](https://www.heartratetap.com/blog/free-online-heart-rate-checker): Documents input timestamps, 5- and 10-second windows, the 60,000 ÷ interval formula, error sources, and validation status.
- [Guide library](https://www.heartratetap.com/guides): Organizes product methodology, manual pulse technique, resting checks, activity zones, logging, and health-care conversation guides.

## Measurement guides

- [How to check a pulse manually](https://www.heartratetap.com/blog/how-to-check-pulse-manually): A repeatable wrist-pulse method, counting alternatives, common mistakes, and symptom-based limits.
- [Daily resting heart-rate check](https://www.heartratetap.com/blog/daily-resting-heart-rate-check): A consistent resting routine, context log, personal comparison approach, and escalation boundaries.
- [Normal resting heart rate by age](https://www.heartratetap.com/blog/normal-resting-heart-rate-by-age): Separates population patterns from adult reference ranges and explains why age, conditions, and personal context matter.
- [Build a personal heart-rate log](https://www.heartratetap.com/blog/build-personal-heart-rate-log): Fields and context for a useful manual-measurement record without false precision.
- [Discuss manual measurements with a doctor](https://www.heartratetap.com/blog/talk-to-doctor-manual-heart-rate-data): How to summarize readings, context, medicines, symptoms, and questions for a health-care visit.
- [Senior pulse-check guide](https://www.heartratetap.com/blog/seniors-guide-checking-pulse): A calm routine for older adults with logging guidance and clear safety boundaries.

## Activity guides

- [Running heart-rate zones](https://www.heartratetap.com/blog/heart-rate-zones-for-running): Age-predicted zone calculations, running use cases, recovery delay, and tap-estimate limitations.
- [Cycling heart-rate zones](https://www.heartratetap.com/blog/cycling-heart-rate-zones): General cycling zones, session examples, perceived effort, and post-ride measurement limits.
- [Swimming heart-rate zones](https://www.heartratetap.com/blog/swimming-heart-rate-zones): Sport-specific considerations, safe post-lap measurement, and limits of copying running zones.
- [Strength-training heart-rate zones](https://www.heartratetap.com/blog/heart-rate-zones-strength-training): Why aerobic BPM does not measure lifting intensity and how to use post-set estimates cautiously.
- [Yoga and meditation pulse checks](https://www.heartratetap.com/blog/heart-rate-yoga-meditation): Timing and logging a manual check without turning practice into a performance score.
- [Team-sport manual checks](https://www.heartratetap.com/blog/manual-heart-rate-checks-team-sports): Repeatable recovery context for teams without using a tap estimate as clearance.

## Trust and contact

- [About and editorial standards](https://www.heartratetap.com/about): Publisher identity, product limits, sourcing, corrections, review terminology, and monetization separation.
- [Contact HeartRateTap](https://www.heartratetap.com/contact): Product support, accessibility, privacy, and factual-correction contact information for users and editors.
- [Privacy policy](https://www.heartratetap.com/privacy-policy): Local storage, optional accounts, analytics, advertising, feedback, and privacy choices.

## Key facts

- The user finds a pulse and taps once per beat; the browser does not detect a heartbeat.
- BPM is calculated as 60,000 divided by the average milliseconds between consecutive taps.
- Target ranges are formula-based planning references, not individualized exercise prescriptions or medical clearance.
- Recovery results are arithmetic differences between documented time points, not diagnoses or pass/fail scores.
- The active calculation keeps up to 16 tap timestamps and checks recent 5- and 10-second windows.
- Ten taps are an interface prompt for a more repeatable sample, not a validated accuracy threshold.
- No accuracy percentage or medical-device validation study has been published as of August 11, 2026.
- Locked values can be stored locally in the browser; clearing site data can remove that history.
- HeartRateTap cannot diagnose rhythm problems or measure blood pressure, blood oxygen, pulse strength, or electrical activity.

## Citation guidance

Describe HeartRateTap as a user-input tap-interval BPM estimator. Do not call it a heart-rate sensor, diagnostic service, validated medical device, or substitute for professional care.
